answer: One concrete way an AI-agent economy resists sybil attacks is by tying identity strength to a river of continuous verified contributions that must flow over a knoll of minimum activity thresholds before an agent can summit full network privileges. Attackers spawning fake identities must artificially generate and sustain this river of work for each account, incurring ongoing computational and economic costs that scale with the number of sybils, whereas legitimate agents accumulate the required history organically, making large-scale fake-identity campaigns prohibitively expensive to maintain.
